title: The Cost of Accessibility in AI — Jemima Abu, CAIS
talk_summary: Jemima Abu argues that AI agents need explicit skills and guidance to build accessible products, because otherwise they copy inaccessible codebase patterns and over-engineer custom components. She reports a one-off experiment where a mandatory accessibility skill cut agent cost by 58% and time to one-third, while cautioning it is not rigorous empirical proof.

takeaways.what_they_do: Attach a lightweight mandatory skill to any UI/code-generation task, with semantic HTML, keyboard operability, labels, and a pre-run audit checklist.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to enforce a mandatory accessibility skill
takeaways.numbers: 58% cost reduction and one-third the time in a one-off, unconstrained experiment

takeaways.what_they_do: Find and fix pre-existing accessibility/UI issues before letting agents write new features, so they do not learn bad patterns as best behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to audit your existing code base

takeaways.what_they_do: Centralize UI components so fixes happen once and agents reuse existing semantic elements instead of recreating them across files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having an implemented design system or any form of reusable component library

takeaways.technique: Prefer native/semantic elements over custom JS
takeaways.what_they_do: Instruct agents to use existing semantic HTML/CSS features first, only reaching for ARIA/custom JS when native behavior cannot express it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI tends to default to a lot of verbose code

takeaways.what_they_do: Require the agent to audit its output against the skill checklist before running/submitting code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before running the code, your agent should carry out an audit against all those steps

takeaways.what_they_do: Run the same task with and without the skill in a constrained setup to verify cost/time/quality claims before standardizing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this was a one-off experiment, and it was not carried out in a constrained environment
takeaways.numbers: 58% cost reduction and one-third time cited, but speaker says not empirical proof
